title: A stray byte in a DNA text halves the key
body:
`Packing::from_occupancy` in `libsufr/src/build.rs` (named `PrefixEncoder` until 75d429b) sets the bits per rank from the number of distinct bytes in the whole text, rounded up to a power of two, and the key holds 64 divided by that many characters. On a DNA text of A, C, G, T, N, the sentinel and the delimiter that is 3 bits and 21 characters. One stray byte past the eighth makes it 4 bits and 16 characters; past the sixteenth, 5 bits and 12; past the thirty-second, 6 bits and 10.

On 2026-11-06 a concatenation of 5,000 bacterial genomes carried about sixty header bytes glued into one sequence by a file with no trailing newline. The text had over 32 distinct bytes, the key fell to 10 characters, a 12-of-17 mask was refused, and the unmasked build left far more ties to the merge sort.

## Proposal

Options, each with its cost:

- Leave it, and let the refusal message say which bytes are in the text, so the cause is visible. Costs nothing and fixes nothing.
- Under `--dna`, rank only A, C, G, T, N, the sentinel and the delimiter, and give every other byte one shared rank. The key stays at 21 characters whatever the text holds. Bytes that share a rank are not ordered by the key, so a tie run may hold suffixes that differ at a key position. `UnmaskedKeys::order_ties` orders such a run by the text through the merge sort. The LCP that `sort_partition` reads off two unequal keys could still overcount. `MaskedKeys::order_ties` never compares the text and assumes that equal masked keys agree at every care position, so it would be wrong for those suffixes. That needs a rule for the shared rank, such as treating it as a tie that `MaskedKeys::order_ties` refuses or sends to the merge sort.
- Drop suffixes starting with those bytes. Under `--dna` this already happens: `keep_table` indexes only suffixes starting with A, C, G, T or the sentinel, since 3944856 removed `--allow-ambiguity`. The bytes inside suffixes still widen the alphabet, so this alone does not help.

## Open

Whether real inputs other than a bad concatenation carry such bytes: IUPAC codes beyond N are common in assemblies.
